title: Why Did the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool Turn Green?
summary: Imagine walking by the famous Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and seeing it glow bright green—like a giant lime slushy! That's what happened this week in Washington, D.C. Just weeks after President Trump had the pool's bottom repainted "American flag blue," it turned a shocking shade of green. Why? Algae! Algae are tiny plants that grow in water. Scientists say this was totally expected. "It's called 'New Pond Syndrome,'" said Steve Goodale, a swimming pool expert. When you fill a big, outdoor pool with fresh water, algae often show up fast. The Reflecting Pool is huge—over 2,000 feet long and as big as about six football fields. That's a lot of water to turn green! A scientist named Rosalina Stancheva Christova tested the water and found a common, harmless type of algae. She said the pool is perfect for algae because it's shallow, still, and gets lots of sun. The new dark blue paint made things worse by soaking up more heat, making the water warmer. The Trump administration says the algae came from old pipes and the very hot weather. Workers are now pouring hydrogen peroxide—a mild cleaner—into the water to kill the algae. They're also using special ozone technology. This isn't the first time the pool has gone green. It happened in 2012 and 2019 too. But this time, it's making headlines because of the recent paint job. So, if you visit D.C. this summer, don't be surprised if the pool looks a little green—it's just nature doing its thing!
why_it_matters: Understanding why algae grows can help you take care of your own small pool or fish tank, and it reminds us that even famous landmarks face ordinary science problems.

background_read: The Lincoln Memorial is a giant statue of Abraham Lincoln, the 16th U.S. president, located in Washington, D.C.
In front of it is the Reflecting Pool, a long, shallow pool that has been a popular spot for visitors and famous protests in American history.
Algae blooms have turned the pool green several times in the past, often after heavy rains or very hot weather.
Article_Structure: WHO: Swimming pool expert Steve Goodale and scientist Rosalina Stancheva Christova, along with workers from the Trump administration.
WHAT: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool turned a shocking bright green because of fast-growing algae.
WHERE: In Washington, D.C., at the famous Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
WHY: The algae growth was expected — 'New Pond Syndrome' happens in big, sunny, still pools with fresh water, and the dark blue paint made the water warmer, helping the algae.

perspectives.description: The algae is harmless and easy to clean, so visitors don't need to worry about their health or the monument.
Some people think the Trump administration's decision to paint the pool dark blue may have made the problem worse, creating extra work.
Scientists explain this is a normal 'New Pond Syndrome' that happens in big outdoor pools, and it can be fixed with simple treatments like hydrogen peroxide.
